5bd8a33 feat(linker): pool memory governor, commit gate and progress-bounded memory retries - worker lifecycle and scheduling only. With no memory trouble the new code does nothing (process_batch, records and write_artifact unchanged; the published-book file lives outside artifacts/ and checkpoints; the packer excludes only temp names a clean tree never has). A governor abort or kill resumes the book from its committed shards through the existing checkpoint contract, and the commit gate (sys.monitoring RAISE + taint) guarantees nothing computed after any MemoryError or abort in a worker image is ever written. Reviewed by three adversarial QA passes (the last verdict: output-neutral yes). No change to normalization, resolution, ambiguity policy, link records or artifact bytes.

5bd8a33 (pool memory governor, commit gate and progress-bounded memory retries; worker lifecycle and scheduling only, reviewed in the 9aef39ad28a5e160 -> 3c529f8ff4f6bcd2 entry) plus one sefaria_resolver.patch hunk: MatchTemplateTrie._merge_two_tries returns a new dict instead of merging into the live, process-wide title trie. The in-place merge ran in a PYTHONHASHSEED-dependent PREFIXES order and, under a bad seed, grew leaf lists compoundingly within one worker life: the resolve memory blow-up of 36072909683. On a pristine trie the new merge returns exactly what the old one returned (50k random tries, inputs never mutated). Verified on the runner with the exact raw-NER spans of 36072909683: unpatched under seeds 26 and 78, and patched under seeds 2 and 26, all four arms produced identical links (30 books complete in every arm, 67,388 links, 0 diffs over 2,716 common batches; 22 complete books byte-identical to that run's own output; peak 0.52 GB), while seed 2 unpatched exploded in 10/10 books; 27 local seed replays also gave identical output. relink.yml now pins PYTHONHASHSEED=26 (not a fingerprint component). No change to normalization, resolution results, ambiguity policy, link records or artifact bytes.

perf(linker) context probes for ibid books. Output-neutral by construction: the pinned bulk_link moves ibid history only inside bulk_resolve of the raw citation refs NER found (_update_ibid_history), IbidContext/last_emitted_ref move only on those, and a transport seam keeps only the last refs (the title map is dropped; restoring is idempotent and a no-op before the first entity), so a whole-book stateful pass is a function of the ordered entity lines and of the set of entity counts at its seams. A probe is planned only when the prior book was resolved with context, every prior flag and its seam counts are known, every dropped line had no entity, the entity lines keep their order and the new layout gives the same seam counts; the producer covers the whole book as soon as a probed line has an entity, and the resolver refuses an unescalated probe whose bundle shows one. Each reused line therefore sees exactly the history it was linked under, and an unescalated probe line has no records. tests/test_context_probe.py links the probe and a whole-book stateful pass with a fake that copies the pinned IbidHistory (refs, titles, title map) and gets identical records; a probed citation or a shifted seam that drops a title makes them differ, which escalation and the seam check prevent (the latter found by QA). A QA fuzzer over random books (5 titles, title-keyed and plain ibid lines, failed citations, random inserts/deletes/length changes, BATCH_LINES 1-4 and varying BATCH_CHARS) found 0 differences in about 4,800 probes and refusals. Everything else is planning, the producer layout and the line-baseline format (book files schema 3 with per-line entity flags, book_context and ibid_seams; the manifest stays at 2). No change to normalization, resolution, ambiguity policy, link records or artifact bytes.
